doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Working with Tatum, Minton's, and the only woman who made him practice
summary: They played cutting contests at Minton's; Tatum said she was the only woman who made him practice and she thinks he may have borrowed ideas from her.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Were there any things beyond his playing that he taught you, taught you about the business or about booking or promoting yourself?
No, he never discussed his bookings. He was just good to be around. I always found him very informative, you know. And I was glad to be around him.
Specifically, what did he show you that you incorporated into your playing?
All the other things that I told you about.
How long did you really work with Art Tatum?
I worked with him in Chicago and worked with him in New York. I used to go up to Minton’s and we’d have cutting contests up there. And eat chicken and waffles and sausage.
Was Tatum a competitive player or was he so far beyond everyone else that he had nothing to worry about?
He had nothing to worry about. As a matter of fact, he didn’t have to compete, he’d just play. One musician said, “God is in the house.” He could cut us with one hand.
Tatum is reported as saying, “Dorothy is the only woman who can make me practice.”
That’s true.
Did he say that to you?
Yeah. And made Hazel Scott leave the country.
Now, his comment, “Dorothy is the only woman who can make me practice,” was that a compliment or is that a little bit of a back-handed insult?
Well, I guess it’s both but I like the compliment.
Do you believe that he would say that there’s any man that could make him practice?
He didn’t think about them too much. He wasn’t worried. There was Billy Taylor and who else during that time? And Oscar [Peterson].
Do you think that there’s anything that you might have shown Tatum that he might have lifted and worked into his playing?
Possibly. Well, see, I never play a piece the same way. So maybe some of my pieces he may have caught things that I didn’t know he was listening for.
According to my notes, this would have been 1943, around the age of 21 for you. Is that about right?
Yes.
